events.title: Röntgen Discovers X-rays
events.description: German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, working at the University of Würzburg, noticed a fluorescent glow on a screen near a shielded cathode-ray tube and identified a new kind of penetrating radiation, which he called X-rays.
events.significance: The discovery revolutionized medicine through diagnostic imaging and opened the way to modern physics. Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

events.title: Beer Hall Putsch Begins
events.description: Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party attempted to seize power in Bavaria by storming a political meeting at the Bürgerbräukeller in Munich on the evening of November 8. The coup attempt collapsed the following day when police fired on marchers.
events.significance: The failed putsch led to Hitler's trial and imprisonment, during which he wrote Mein Kampf, and it taught him to pursue power through legal and electoral means, shaping the Nazi rise in the early 1930s.

John F. Kennedy Elected President
events.description: Democratic Senator John F. Kennedy of Massachusetts defeated Vice President Richard Nixon in one of the closest presidential elections in U.S. history, becoming the youngest person elected to the presidency at age 43 and the first Catholic.
events.significance: Kennedy's election marked a generational shift in American politics, and the campaign featured the first televised presidential debates, which changed the role of media in elections.

events.title: First Jet-to-Jet Dogfight
events.description: During the Korean War, U.S. Air Force Lt. Russell J. Brown, flying an F-80 Shooting Star, shot down a North Korean MiG-15 in the first air-to-air combat between jet aircraft.
events.significance: The engagement marked the beginning of the jet age in aerial warfare and signaled the end of propeller-driven fighters as the dominant combat aircraft.
